# Audit: HugeThings settings localization repair, before the fourth live run

**Verdict:** The C# should compile, and the local search and reset are behaviourally the same as the shared helpers, with one item to confirm (2). Two proof gaps should be closed before the fourth run, because the rendered English text cannot show that these strings now come from `Translate`.

## 1. Compile risk (TaggedString and `??`): low

- **`tagOverride ?? (cond ? "A".Translate() : ...)`.** Both ternary branches are `TaggedString`, so the ternary is `TaggedString`. `tagOverride` is `string`. C# picks `string` as the result because `TaggedString` converts implicitly to `string`, and that rule is checked first. `list.Label(string, …)` then binds directly, so there is no ambiguity.
- **Call sites.** These pass `.Translate()` into the `string tagOverride` and `string title` parameters. The `RM_HugeThings_GiantPlants` header already does this, so it is a known-good pattern.
- **`TextEntryLabeled(...)` and `ButtonText(...)`.** Both receive the label through the same implicit conversion, which is fine.
- **One check.** If `Group`'s `tagOverride` parameter is declared as `TaggedString` rather than `string`, the result type flips but it still compiles. Look at the signature once.

## 2. Is the local search/reset replacement faithful?

- **Search.** It is byte-for-byte the same call: `TextEntryLabeled(label, query ?? "")` with the same default line count.
- **Reset.** It is equivalent. The shared helper ran `onReset` only when the button was pressed and the callback was non-null. `ResetFields(names)` is always non-null, and the dropped bool return was unused.
- **Scope line: confirm this one.** The old text was `SettingsKitCore.ScopeTag(scope) + " changes …"`. The new keys hard-code the prefixes `[now]`, `[next pulse]` and `[new maps only]`. Read `ScopeTag` and confirm it returns exactly those three strings, including spacing and case. If `ScopeTag(Now)` returned `""` or `"[now] "`, the visible text changed. The live label check would catch that as a mismatch, but better to know before the run.
- **Collapse state.** If `Group` stores collapse state keyed by title, the key is now localized. That is harmless in English. It matters only if the collapsed set is saved to the settings file, in which case changing language would reset it. This is minor; note it rather than fix it.

## 3. Strings still possibly unkeyed on this path

From the diff alone I can't rule out the following. Grep for them:

- **The body of `Group(...)`** above line 461: the `"- "`/`"+ "` markers (not language text, acceptable) and any "no matches" or hint text.
- **`SettingsCategory()`.** It probably returns a literal "Huge Things", which is the visible window title and mod-list entry. Decide explicitly whether it counts as a "settings label". I would key it or record the exemption.
- **Concatenations** such as `": "` and `" x"` inside unchanged label lines.
- **Duplicate keys.** Confirm the 13 new keys don't already exist in any other `Keyed/*.xml` in the mod. A duplicate is a config error, which your startup-log scan would catch, but only after deployment.

## 4. Missing checks for this repair (the main point)

**(a) The UI cannot tell keyed text from hard-coded text.** The English values are identical to the old literals, so `label_checks` passes the same before and after the repair. The judge needs one or both of:

- **A source gate**, added to `selftest_settings_hardening.py`. Within `DoSettingsWindowContents` and `Group`, every string literal must fall into one of these categories:
  - followed by `.Translate(`;
  - inside a `new[] { … }` field-name array;
  - a `ToString` format;
  - on an explicit allowlist (`"- "`, `"+ "`, `""`).

  Fail on any other literal. Also assert that `SettingsKitDrawer.` and `SettingsKitCore.ScopeTag` no longer appear in this file.
- **A deployed-DLL check.** In the user-string heap of the deployed `HugeThings.dll` (sha-tied to the build stamp), each of the 13 new key names must be present. The removed literals must be absent: "Large Pawns footprint and custom size tiers", "Wake and plant smashing", "Turn on giant animals to change these.", " changes apply to what is on the map now".

  "Reset this section to defaults" and "Search settings" will still be present, because `SettingsKitDrawer.cs` is still linked by `<Compile Include>`. Exempt those two, or the check gives a false fail.

**(b) Keys that are never rendered are not proven.** `RM_HugeThings_NeedsAnimals` and `RM_HugeThings_ScopeNewMaps` are excluded from the UI checks, because animals are on and no group uses the new-maps scope. A missing XML entry for either would render raw and go unseen. Add a static cross-check in both directions:

- every `"RM_HugeThings_*".Translate(` key in the source exists in the Keyed XML;
- every new XML key is referenced in the source.

If `ScopeNewMaps` has no caller, you can keep it as a defensive branch, but state that it is dead.

**(c) Small script notes.**

- The key regex does catch `ScopeNextStart`, since it is a literal followed by `.Translate(` used as an argument, so that one is covered.
- Confirm that the layout reports a label for the `TextEntryLabeled` caption and for the reset `ButtonText`. If it doesn't, `SearchSettings` and `ResetSection` fail as "missing", which would be an oracle defect, not a product defect. Your previous run passed with the shared helpers drawing those same texts, which suggests both are captured.

## 5. Bounded advice before the fourth run

1. Read `ScopeTag` and the `Group` and `SettingsCategory` bodies, and resolve items 2 and 3.
2. Add the source-literal gate and the source/XML two-way key check to the selftest. Run it offline and have it fail against the pre-repair source, to show it detects the old violation.
3. After the build, run the DLL user-string check against the exact artifact you will deploy, and record its sha next to the stamp.
4. Keep the live run unchanged: same arms, same 14-mod/five-DLC tier, same restoration. Its job is to show no regression and no raw keys. Tell the judge plainly that it **cannot by itself** prove the strings go through `Translate`. Steps 2 and 3 provide that proof.
5. Keep the existing disclosures (work-hours `.25` renders as `0.3`; numeric/Scribe/Sanitize prefix bytes unchanged), and add "Shared drawer still linked; its English literals remain in the DLL but are unused on this path."
